events.description: "Komatsu's first laser cladding cell, delivered on time and on budget, is now in operation."
Laserbond "signed a second licensing agreement with Komatsu... covering a second modular laser cladding cell for Komatsu’s Perth facility."
The first Komatsu agreement, "signed in August 2025 and valued at $2.4 million," delivered a cell that "is now in operation."
Laserbond entered a Collaboration Agreement with Metal 7 under which Metal 7 owns customer relationships while Laserbond retains and licenses its intellectual property.
The second agreement "provides for a second modular laser cladding cell at Komatsu's Perth facility, due for delivery in FY27."
Laserbond "executed its first licensing agreement with Komatsu in August 2025" and "the agreement was valued at $2.4 million."
Komatsu's first laser cell was "completed on time and on budget, and site operation has commenced."
“Komatsu licensing deal confirms blue-chip commercial credibility,” with the investment-case slide stating that “Komatsu [is] signed.”
“Further global laser cell opportunities, with discussions underway for additional cells in new markets.”
A modular laser cell for Komatsu was completed on time and on budget and passed factory acceptance in June 2026, with site operation to commence in Q1 FY27.

The Komatsu licensing agreement reached a key milestone with the first modular laser cell passing factory acceptance in June 2026 and commissioning completed, with site operation to begin in Australia in Q1 FY27.
Further laser cell projects progressed through development, with additional contracts expected in FY27 and discussions underway on cells in other regions.
“The Komatsu licensing agreement, valued at $2.4 million, provides independent validation of this technology from a blue-chip global customer.”
“Commissioning of the cell has since been completed, with site operation to commence in Australia during Q1 FY27.”
